datasets.name: bnr-currencies
datasets.title: Currencies with a reference rate of the National Bank of Romania
datasets.description: The currencies for which the National Bank of Romania (BNR) publishes a reference rate against the leu, with the number of units the rate is given for and the first and last day of publication, from 2005. XAU is one gram of gold and XDR is the special drawing right. A currency BNR stopped publishing stays in the list with its last day. The rates themselves are not here: read them from BNR.

source.name: National Bank of Romania, yearly reference rate files
source.licence: Facts taken from the files; no rate is copied. BNR's own terms for its content: https://www.bnr.ro/2281-termeni-si-conditii

datasets.update: When BNR adds a currency, stops publishing one or changes a multiplier

fields.name: code
fields.description: The currency code of BNR, three letters, as in ISO 4217

fields.name: multiplier
fields.description: The number of units the rate is given for: the rate of HUF is for 100 forints

fields.name: valid_from
fields.description: The first day BNR published a rate with this multiplier, as YYYY-MM-DD; not before 2005-01-03, the first day of the files

fields.name: valid_to
fields.description: The last day BNR published a rate, as YYYY-MM-DD, or null while it still does

datasets.name: countries
datasets.title: Countries and territories
datasets.description: Countries and territories with their ISO 3166-1 codes, their names in Romanian and English, and whether they are a member state of the European Union today. Withdrawn entries stay, with their last day of use, so an alpha-2 code can appear on a withdrawn entry and on a current one; the alpha-3 code is unique. Kosovo is not in ISO 3166-1 and is listed with the user-assigned codes XK and XKX. Names are the short names the European Union institutions use, with Romanian letters written with the comma below and without the asterisk the source puts on Kosovo. A name does not state a position on the status of a territory.

source.name: Publications Office of the European Union, Countries and territories authority table
source.licence: European Commission reuse notice (Decision 2011/833/EU): reuse allowed with the source acknowledged

datasets.update: When the Publications Office changes the table: a new or withdrawn country, a changed name, a change in the European Union

fields.name: alpha2
fields.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code; for Kosovo the user-assigned XK

fields.name: alpha3
fields.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code, unique in the file; for Kosovo the user-assigned XKX

fields.name: numeric
fields.description: ISO 3166-1 numeric code, three digits, or null when the source gives none

fields.name: name_ro
fields.description: Short name in Romanian

fields.name: name_en
fields.description: Short name in English

fields.name: eu_member
fields.description: True for a member state of the European Union at the time of the build

fields.name: iso
fields.description: False for an entry ISO 3166-1 does not list

fields.name: valid_from
fields.description: The first day of use the source gives, as YYYY-MM-DD. Many old entries carry 1950-05-09, the first day of the table

fields.name: valid_to
fields.description: The last day of use of a withdrawn entry, as YYYY-MM-DD, or null for a current one

datasets.name: public-holidays
datasets.title: Public holidays of Romania
datasets.description: The days on which no work is done by law, as rules that give the days of any year: a fixed month and day, or a number of days from Orthodox Easter Sunday. Orthodox Easter Sunday is the Julian computus moved to the civil calendar. A day can come from two rules, such as the second day of Pentecost on 1 June. Days declared free by a Government decision for one year only are not included. The two days each of three yearly feasts of other legal religions have no fixed date and are not included.

source.name: Labour Code (Law 53/2003, republished), article 139 (1); Orthodox Easter is computed
source.licence: Romanian legislation, not subject to copyright (Law 8/1996, article 9)

datasets.update: When article 139 of the Labour Code changes

fields.name: name
fields.description: The name of the holiday, in Romanian

fields.name: rule
fields.description: fixed: the same month and day every year. orthodox-easter-offset: a number of days from Orthodox Easter Sunday

fields.name: month
fields.description: The month, 1 to 12, of a fixed rule; null otherwise

fields.name: day
fields.description: The day of the month of a fixed rule; null otherwise

fields.name: easter_offset
fields.description: Days from Orthodox Easter Sunday, negative before it; null for a fixed rule

fields.name: valid_from
fields.description: The first day this dataset vouches for the rule, as YYYY-MM-DD. Not the day the holiday became law

fields.name: valid_to
fields.description: The last day of the rule, as YYYY-MM-DD, or null while it is in force
